channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan Vice President Karin Discusses Cooperation with Religious Leaders Ahead of Astana Congress
item.description: Kazakhstan's Vice President Yerlan Karin met with representatives of Muslim and Christian organizations to discuss religious education, interfaith dialogue, and preparations for the upcoming Congress of Leaders of World and Traditional Religions in Astana. Karin emphasized the importance of their contributions to promoting peace and mutual respect.

item.title: Turkmenistan Introduces E-Visa System Amidst Uncertainty for Foreign Visitors
item.description: Turkmenistan has launched an online visa system to simplify travel for foreigners, though details remain unclear for visiting the highly closed country. The State Migration Service briefed diplomats on the new electronic visa and registration systems, aiming to streamline processes and increase efficiency.

item.title: Yerlan Karin Holds Meetings with Religious Leaders Ahead of Congress in Astana
item.description: Kazakhstan's Vice President Yerlan Karin held bilateral meetings with religious leaders as part of the XXIV session of the Secretariat of the Congress of Leaders of World and Traditional Religions. Discussions focused on the agenda of the upcoming session and further cooperation within the forum.

item.title: Kazakhstan Discusses Religious Education Cooperation with Al-Azhar
item.description: Kazakhstan's Vice President Yerlan Karin met with Abdulrahman Musa, advisor to the Grand Imam of Al-Azhar, to discuss cooperation in religious education and interfaith dialogue. The meeting occurred during the XXIV session of the Secretariat of the Congress of Leaders of World and Traditional Religions. Discussions also covered collaboration with other religious organizations.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Iran Discuss Strengthening Bilateral Cooperation
item.description: Uzbekistan's First Deputy Foreign Minister Bahromjon Alov met with Iran's Ambassador to Uzbekistan Mohammad Ali Eskandari to discuss strengthening cooperation. Key areas of focus included political, trade-economic, transport, and cultural-humanitarian spheres. Both sides confirmed their interest in expanding practical interaction and bilateral ties.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Increase Electricity Consumption Norm for Unheated Areas in Winter
item.description: Uzbekistan will raise the basic electricity consumption norm for unheated and gas-unsupplied areas to 350 kWh per month during winter. This measure, approved by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, aims to support households during the cold season. The proposal also includes extending subsidies for excess energy consumption until April 2028.

item.title: Uzbekistan and India Expand Cooperation in Tourism Sector
item.description: Uzbekistan and India are enhancing tourism cooperation, with a business forum and B2B meetings held in Tashkent. Discussions focused on increasing mutual tourist flow, developing direct business contacts, and creating new joint products. The event supported the launch of direct flights between Tashkent and Hyderabad.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ratifies European Convention to Aid Recovery of Illicit Assets
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev signed a law ratifying the European Convention on Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters. This enhances Kazakhstan's ability to search, seize, and recover assets illegally transferred to European countries. The convention facilitates evidence gathering and cooperation in criminal investigations.

item.title: UN to Cooperate with Pakistan on Voluntary, Dignified Return of Afghan Migrants
item.description: UN Secretary-General António Guterres stated the UN will cooperate with Pakistan to ensure the voluntary, safe, and dignified return of Afghan migrants. Guterres acknowledged Pakistan's decades-long hospitality to Afghan refugees and emphasized support for those seeking safety. Pakistan began expelling Afghan migrants in 2023.

item.title: Kazakh Citizens Await Aid Amidst Reports of Forced Mobilization in Russia
item.description: Kazakh citizens reportedly face forced mobilization for war in Russia and are awaiting assistance from Kazakh authorities. Separately, the former commander of the Air and Sea Forces was arrested in connection with deaths on the Caspian Sea. Another case has been initiated against Sanzhar Bokaev and his associates.

item.title: Turkey and Pakistan to Deploy Troops to Saudi Arabia Against Houthis Under Defense Pact
item.description: Turkey and Pakistan will urgently send troops to Saudi Arabia to combat Houthis, based on the Mecca defense agreement. This decision follows escalating Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia from Yemen. The deployment aims to bolster the Kingdom's defense capabilities against the ongoing regional conflict.

item.title: Taliban Report 860 People, Including 202 Families, Returned to Afghanistan Yesterday
item.description: The Taliban announced that 860 individuals from 202 families were returned to Afghanistan via various routes yesterday. Hamdullah Fitrat, deputy spokesperson, stated that 525 people from 125 families entered through Nimruz. Returns continue despite challenges like lack of shelter and necessities as winter approaches.

item.title: Drought and Salt-Resistant Tree Cultivation Begins in Kazakhstan
item.description: Kazakhstan has begun cultivating Turanga, a tree species resistant to drought and saline soils, suitable for arid regions. Specialists have developed a laboratory technology for mass propagation to restore degraded lands. The tree is being planted in reserves and planned for new green zones.

item.title: Atyrau Oil Refinery Inspected After Air Quality Complaints, Materials Sent to Law Enforcement
item.description: Following public complaints about air quality, the Atyrau Oil Refinery underwent an unscheduled inspection. The inspection revealed violations of environmental requirements, including uncalculated emissions and unestablished permitted emission standards for several units. The refinery also experienced emergency gas flaring incidents.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ratifies European Convention on Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters
item.description: Kazakhstan has ratified the European Convention on Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters. The ratification, signed by President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, aims to enhance cooperation between Kazakh law enforcement and European states. This will facilitate evidence gathering and the return of assets illegally transferred abroad, especially where bilateral agreements are lacking.

item.title: Violations Detected at Atyrau Oil Refinery Following Resident Complaints
item.description: An unscheduled inspection at the Atyrau oil refinery revealed violations after residents complained about air quality. The inspection found uncalculated emissions and unestablished permitted norms at several facilities. Emergency situations on August 25 and September 2-7 resulted in over 100 tons of gas being flared.

item.title: Uzbekistan Enhances Water Resource Management for Autumn-Winter Season
item.description: Navoiy region in Uzbekistan is implementing measures to optimize water resource use for the 2026-2027 autumn-winter season. Efforts include cleaning irrigation networks and repairing hydraulic structures. Specialists emphasize efficient water use is crucial for agricultural production, food security, and regional economic development in water-scarce areas.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Increasing Electricity Norm for Gasless Regions During Heating Season
item.description: Uzbekistan proposes raising the basic electricity consumption norm for regions without gas supply during the heating season. An extension until April 1, 2028, is also suggested for covering a portion of expenses exceeding the basic norm for electricity and gas consumption. Details are available on Daryo.uz.

item.title: Uzbekistan Prioritizes Child Protection with New Strategy and Legal Reforms
item.description: Uzbekistan has elevated child protection to a state policy priority, enacting reforms to safeguard children from violence, discrimination, and exploitation. The adoption of the Child Protection Strategy for 2026-2030 and amendments to various legal codes aim to enhance prevention, early detection, and support for child victims, fostering inter-agency and public cooperation.

item.title: Global Dialogue on Future in AI Era to Convene in Almaty at BE WOMAN ASIA 2026 Forum
item.description: The BE WOMAN ASIA 2026 forum will gather leaders from science, business, technology, and culture across 25 countries in Almaty on October 15th. The event, themed "Ethical Power," will explore accountability for AI-driven decisions. Notable speakers include a co-creator of the first graphical web browser and a two-time Oscar winner.

item.title: Moscow Format Meeting Concludes Without Joint Statement Amid Taliban-Pakistan Disagreements
item.description: The eighth Moscow Format meeting concluded without a joint statement due to disagreements between the Taliban and Pakistan concerning security and militant groups. This episode delves into the dispute and its implications for regional diplomacy, featuring insights from a university lecturer and a military affairs analyst.

item.title: Iranian General's Remarks on Smartwatches Raise Security Concerns
item.description: An Iranian general's response to questions about wearing a smartwatch has amplified security concerns. Brigadier General Gholamreza Jalali dismissed fears that smart devices could be used to track high-ranking officials, even during wartime. This comes amid heightened tensions and past security breaches in Iran.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Communal Enterprise Fined 174 Million Tenge for Illegal Wastewater Discharge
item.description: A communal enterprise in Petropavl has been fined 174 million Tenge for illegally discharging wastewater. The North Kazakhstan region's prosecutor's office reported that the nature protection prosecutor discovered the violation. An inspection revealed the enterprise discharged wastewater without proper authorization. The court issued the ruling for the fine.

item.title: UN Official Highlights Drought, Aid Cuts, and Migration Challenges in Afghanistan
item.description: A UN official cited severe drought, water management issues, large-scale migrant returns, and border closures as major challenges in southern Afghanistan. He noted that declining international aid exacerbates pressure on local communities. Farmers struggle with alternative crops, potentially returning to poppy cultivation if support remains inadequate, the UN official warned.

item.title: Kazakhstan Amends Early Retirement Pension Annuity Rules Effective October 2026
item.description: Kazakhstan will introduce changes to its model pension annuity contract starting October 16, 2026. The Agency for Regulation and Development of the Financial Market has clarified requirements regarding funding sources and heirs, and strengthened insurers' liability for delayed payments. The annuity allows individuals to receive regular monthly payments from their pension savings.

item.title: UN Agencies Provide Aid to Over 3 Million People in Northern Afghanistan
item.description: A joint program involving 12 UN agencies has delivered humanitarian and development assistance to over three million people in five northern Afghan provinces. Women and girls constituted 53% of beneficiaries. The aid focused on basic services, health, psychosocial support, livelihoods, business support, and climate resilience programs.

item.title: Violations Found at Atyrau Refinery After Air Quality Complaints
item.description: An unscheduled inspection at the Atyrau Oil Refinery in Kazakhstan revealed violations of environmental requirements following numerous complaints from residents about air quality. The Ministry of Ecology reported that the plant failed to calculate emissions and set permissible limits for some equipment. Gas was flared due to accidents, exceeding emission standards for certain pollutants.

item.title: Kazakh scientists develop technology to purify water and soil by over 99%
item.description: Scientists at Satbayev University have developed technologies to remove heavy metals, radioactive elements, and organic pollutants from water and soil. Using cold plasma, they can destroy complex organic substances, achieving over 99% removal of a model pollutant in about 30 minutes. Biochar is used to restore contaminated soils by retaining and reducing the mobility of metals like copper, zinc, cadmium, and lead.

item.title: Kazakhstan seeks Indian Ocean railway access via Afghanistan and Pakistan
item.description: Kazakhstan is pursuing a railway route to the Indian Ocean through Afghanistan and Pakistan, aiming to leverage existing trade, particularly its $573 million in exports to Afghanistan in early 2026. Recent developments include a trilateral agreement with Uzbekistan and UAE to study a corridor via Afghanistan, and the opening of a new railway section in western Afghanistan involving a Kazakh company.

item.title: Taliban Foreign Minister discusses expanding cooperation with Russian Deputy Prime Minister
item.description: Taliban Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi met with Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexey Overchuk in Moscow to discuss expanding bilateral cooperation. Discussions covered economic, trade, transit, energy, and political cooperation, with a call for facilitating banking services. Russia expressed readiness to expand economic ties and cooperation in transit, transportation, and energy sectors.

item.title: National Resistance Front: Taliban and ISIS are ideologically similar, 'two sides of the same coin'
item.description: Afghanistan's National Resistance Front (NRF) has condemned ISIS, stating that the Taliban and ISIS are ideologically identical and "two sides of the same coin." The NRF claims both groups rely on extremism and violence, contradicting Afghan values, and views rivalries between them as mere power-sharing disputes.

item.title: CASA-1000 project rockfalls make Panjshir's main road dangerous for travelers
item.description: Residents of Panjshir report that ongoing work on the CASA-1000 power transmission project is causing dangerous rockfalls onto the main road. Project officials had promised protective netting, but it has not been installed. The alternative route is unpaved and difficult to use, disrupting daily travel.

item.title: Uzbekistan National Football Team Loses Friendly Match to South Korea
item.description: The Uzbekistan national football team lost their friendly match against South Korea with a score of 0-2. This was the final match played during the September-October FIFA international break. Fabio Cannavaro is the head coach of the national team.

item.title: Kabul attack survivor recounts bombing, recovery, and subsequent university ban
item.description: A survivor of the September 30, 2022, Kaaj Educational Center bombing in Kabul shares her harrowing experience. She details the attack, her recovery, and her success in the national entrance exam, only to be banned from university by the Taliban. The attack killed over 50 people, mostly young women.

item.title: Woman sentenced to six years for defrauding job seekers abroad
item.description: A woman in Kokshetau has been sentenced to six years and eight months in prison for fraud. Operating as an individual entrepreneur and social media blogger, she promised employment abroad, charging between 250,000 and 1 million tenge per client. She defrauded 92 victims of approximately 70 million tenge.

item.title: US State Department Assesses Kazakhstan's Investment Climate Amid Corruption Concerns
item.description: The US State Department has evaluated Kazakhstan's investment climate, citing corruption and unpredictable laws as significant challenges. This assessment highlights concerns that could impact foreign investment and economic development within the Central Asian nation, suggesting a need for regulatory and anti-corruption reforms.

item.title: Kazakhstan President and Sultan of Oman Visit Astana International Financial Center
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and the Sultan of Oman, Haitham bin Tariq Al Said, visited the Astana International Financial Center (AIFC). AIFC управляющий Renat Bektyrov presented the center's achievements, including over $28 billion in attracted investments and more than 6,600 registered companies from 90 countries.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Central Bank Announces New Exchange Rates for October 7
item.description: The Central Bank of Uzbekistan has announced the official exchange rates for foreign currencies against the Uzbek soum, effective October 7. The US dollar saw an increase in its value against the national currency. Further details are available on Daryo.uz.

item.title: Major infrastructure projects underway in Chartak district, Namangan region
item.description: Significant infrastructure development is occurring in Uzbekistan's Chartak district, Namangan region. Projects include the complete reconstruction of a 1974 bridge connecting Uychi and Chartak districts, costing 36 billion UZS. Additionally, the Furkat Culture and Recreation Park is being renovated with World Bank support, costing 34.85 billion UZS, aiming to boost tourism and the local economy.

item.title: Taliban Ministry of Justice Demands Rent from Residents for Their Own Homes
item.description: Residents of Omid-e Sabz Township report that the Taliban's Ministry of Justice is demanding a monthly rent of 4,000 Afghanis per room for houses they own and built themselves. Homeowners claim they are being pressured to pay rent for the past six months and threatened with eviction if they fail to comply with the new directive.
